name: Symplectic integrators ↔ Hamiltonian flow
summary: Leapfrog/Verlet and other symplectic schemes are exact flows of a nearby 'shadow' Hamiltonian, so they preserve phase-space volume and show no secular energy drift; the integrator inherits the symplectic structure of Hamilton's equations.
breaks: Backward-error bound holds only for fixed step size; adaptive steps or dissipation destroy the shadow Hamiltonian.
sources: Verlet (1967). "Computer 'Experiments' on Classical Fluids. I. Thermodynamical Properties of Lennard-Jones Molecules". *Phys. Rev.* 159, 98. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.159.98](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.159.98)

name: DNS and spectral solvers ↔ turbulence
summary: Direct numerical simulation must resolve from the integral scale L down to the Kolmogorov scale η, so grid points grow as Re^{9/4}; pseudospectral FFT methods and LES closures are the workhorses of turbulence research.

name: Normal modes = generalized eigenproblem
summary: Small oscillations about equilibrium reduce to the symmetric generalized eigenproblem Kv = ω²Mv; normal modes are the orthogonal eigenvectors guaranteed by the spectral theorem.

name: Noether's theorem ↔ energy, momentum, angular momentum
summary: The conservation laws of Newtonian mechanics are the Noether charges of time translation, space translation and rotation invariance of the action.
map: \partial L/\partial t=0\Rightarrow E=\dot q\,\partial L/\partial\dot q-L\ \text{conserved}
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Newtonian mechanics as symmetry consequences
summary: The Galilean symmetry group of Newtonian mechanics (translations, rotations, boosts) fixes its conserved quantities; the Galilean boost charge gives uniform centre-of-mass motion.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Buckingham π ↔ Reynolds similarity
summary: Dimensional analysis reduces drag and flow problems to functions of a few dimensionless groups (Re, Ma, Fr), which is the basis of wind-tunnel scaling and dynamic similarity.
sources: Buckingham (1914). "On Physically Similar Systems; Illustrations of the Use of Dimensional Equations". *Phys. Rev.* 4, 345. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.4.345](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.4.345)

name: N-body integrators ↔ celestial mechanics
summary: Long-term Solar System integrations use symplectic map methods (Wisdom–Holman splitting into Kepler drift plus interaction kick) and regularization for close encounters.
map: H=H_{\rm Kep}+H_{\rm int},\ \ e^{hL_H}\approx e^{\frac h2L_{\rm int}}e^{hL_{\rm Kep}}e^{\frac h2L_{\rm int}}

name: Force Concept Inventory ↔ Newton's laws
summary: Newton's three laws are the content probed by the Force Concept Inventory; PER shows students hold impetus-like preconceptions, and interactive engagement roughly doubles the normalized gain.
sources: Hestenes, Wells & Swackhamer (1992). "Force concept inventory". *Phys. Teach.* 30, 141. [doi:10.1119/1.2343497](https://doi.org/10.1119/1.2343497)

Hake (1998). "Interactive-engagement versus traditional methods: A six-thousand-student survey of mechanics test data for introductory physics courses". *Am. J. Phys.* 66, 64. [doi:10.1119/1.18809](https://doi.org/10.1119/1.18809)

name: Rotation group SO(3) ↔ rigid-body motion
summary: A rigid body's configuration space is SO(3); Euler's equations are the Lie–Poisson equations on so(3)*, and the inertia tensor defines a left-invariant metric whose geodesics are torque-free motions.

name: Invariance of the action → Noether currents
summary: Noether's theorem is a statement about the variational principle: a continuous transformation leaving the action invariant up to a boundary term yields a conserved quantity; cyclic coordinates are the simplest case.
map: \delta L=\frac{dK}{dt}\Rightarrow Q=\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot q}\delta q-K,\ \dot Q=0
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Phase space as a symplectic manifold
summary: Phase space is the cotangent bundle T*Q with symplectic 2-form ω = dp∧dq; Hamilton's equations are ι_X ω = dH, Poisson brackets come from ω^{-1}, and Liouville's theorem is conservation of the volume form ω^n.

name: Hamilton–Jacobi PDE ↔ method of characteristics
summary: The Hamilton–Jacobi equation is a first-order nonlinear PDE whose characteristics are exactly Hamilton's equations; complete integrals give generating functions of canonical transformations.

name: Standard map = leapfrog kicked rotor
summary: Chirikov's standard map is the symplectic-Euler discretization of a pendulum and the exact flow of the kicked rotor; KAM theory explains why symplectic integrators keep invariant tori and stay stable for exponentially long times.
breaks: Correspondence with the continuous pendulum holds only for small step K; for K≳1 the map's global chaos is a discretization artifact.

name: Lyapunov spectra and shadowing in numerics
summary: Lyapunov exponents are computed by tangent-map integration with repeated QR (Gram–Schmidt) reorthonormalization; the shadowing lemma justifies trusting chaotic numerical orbits statistically even though each diverges from the true one.

name: Lyapunov instability underlies MD ergodicity
summary: Many-particle MD trajectories are chaotic with positive Lyapunov exponents, so individual trajectories are irreproducible after picoseconds while time averages converge to ensemble averages; chaos is what makes MD statistics robust.

name: Pitchfork bifurcation = Landau symmetry breaking
summary: The normal form of a Z2-symmetric pitchfork is gradient flow on a φ⁴ potential; the supercritical branch is mean-field spontaneous symmetry breaking with exponent 1/2.
breaks: No fluctuations or thermodynamic limit, so only mean-field exponents; Hopf bifurcations break time translation rather than an internal symmetry.

name: Principal axes = spectral theorem for the inertia tensor
summary: The inertia tensor is real symmetric, so it has orthogonal eigenvectors (principal axes) and real eigenvalues (principal moments); rotational kinetic energy is diagonal in that basis.

name: Strain compatibility = flat metric; defects = torsion and curvature
summary: Saint-Venant compatibility is the vanishing Riemann tensor of the deformed metric g = δ + 2ε; in the geometric theory of defects dislocations are torsion and disclinations curvature of a material connection.

name: Finite elements born in structural elasticity
summary: The finite element method grew out of structural and elasticity analysis (Courant's 1943 variational triangles, 1950s aircraft stress analysis) and is a Ritz–Galerkin minimization of the elastic energy.

name: Acoustic waves ↔ retarded Green's function
summary: Sound radiated by sources is the source convolved with the retarded Green's function of the wave equation; Huygens' sharp-front principle holds in odd spatial dimensions.

name: Damped oscillator response ↔ causality and Kramers–Kronig
summary: The driven damped oscillator's susceptibility has poles only in the lower half ω-plane because the response is causal, so its real and imaginary parts obey Kramers–Kronig; its impulse response is the retarded Green's function.

name: Floquet theory of the Mathieu equation
summary: Parametric resonance is governed by Floquet–Hill theory of linear ODEs with periodic coefficients; Mathieu characteristic exponents define the instability tongues near ω = 2ω₀/n.

name: KdV hierarchies ↔ infinite-dimensional Lie algebras
summary: Integrable soliton equations come in hierarchies attached to Kac–Moody algebras (Drinfeld–Sokolov); the Lax pair is a flat connection in a loop algebra and tau functions carry representations of infinite-dimensional groups.
sources: Drinfeld & Sokolov (1984). "Lie algebras and equations of Korteweg-de Vries type". *J. Sov. Math.* 30, 1975. [doi:10.1007/bf02105860](https://doi.org/10.1007/bf02105860)
Jimbo & Miwa (1983). "Solitons and Infinite Dimensional Lie Algebras". *Publ. RIMS Kyoto* 19, 943. [doi:10.2977/prims/1195182017](https://doi.org/10.2977/prims/1195182017)

name: Inverse scattering via analytic scattering data
summary: The inverse scattering transform solves KdV and NLS by mapping initial data to scattering data analytic in the spectral parameter, reconstructed through a Riemann–Hilbert (Gelfand–Levitan) problem; solitons are bound-state poles.

name: Integrability = enough conserved charges in involution
summary: Liouville–Arnold integrability needs n Poisson-commuting conserved quantities; KdV has infinitely many, generated by commuting symmetry flows, which is why solitons survive collisions.

name: Small divisors and analytic estimates in KAM
summary: Lindstedt perturbation series diverge because of small denominators k·ω; KAM proves torus survival for Diophantine frequencies by Newton iteration with Cauchy estimates on shrinking complex analyticity strips.

name: Physics-informed networks for Navier–Stokes
summary: PINNs penalize the Navier–Stokes residual in the loss to reconstruct velocity and pressure from sparse data; flow problems are the main testbed for scientific-ML surrogates.
sources: Cai et al. (2021). "Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for fluid mechanics: a review". *Acta Mech. Sin.* 37, 1727. [arXiv:2105.09506](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09506)

Raissi, Perdikaris & Karniadakis (2019). "Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear partial differential equations". *J. Comput. Phys.* 378, 686. [doi:10.1016/j.jcp.2018.10.045](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2018.10.045)

name: Kolmogorov 1941 from dimensional analysis
summary: If the inertial range depends only on the dissipation rate ε and wavenumber k, dimensional analysis fixes the −5/3 spectrum and the Kolmogorov scale; intermittency corrections are the anomalous part beyond dimensional reasoning.

name: Re ≪ 1 regime and the scallop theorem
summary: At Re ≪ 1 inertia drops out and Stokes flow is linear and instantaneous, so reciprocal strokes give no net swimming (Purcell's scallop theorem); scaling arguments set what microswimmers can do.
sources: Purcell (1977). "Life at low Reynolds number". *Am. J. Phys.* 45, 3. [doi:10.1119/1.10903](https://doi.org/10.1119/1.10903)

name: Stokeslet = Green's function of Stokes flow
summary: The Oseen tensor (Stokeslet) is the Green's function of the Stokes equations; boundary-integral, slender-body and hydrodynamic-interaction methods superpose it.

name: Kepler's hidden SO(4) and the Runge–Lenz vector
summary: The conserved Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector together with L generates SO(4) for bound Kepler orbits, explaining closed ellipses (Bertrand) and, once quantized, the n² degeneracy of hydrogen (Pauli 1926).

name: Rutherford scattering discovered the nucleus
summary: Rutherford's classical Coulomb-orbit cross-section, fitted to Geiger–Marsden α data, revealed the atomic nucleus; the same formula happens to be exact in quantum mechanics.
sources: Rutherford (1911). "The scattering of α and β particles by matter and the structure of the atom". *Phil. Mag.* 21, 669. [doi:10.1080/14786440508637080](https://doi.org/10.1080/14786440508637080)

name: Fictitious forces as connection coefficients
summary: Coriolis and centrifugal forces are the Christoffel symbols of rotating coordinates in flat space; writing Newton's law covariantly prefigures the equivalence principle.

name: Poisson brackets ↔ commutators; Koopman–von Neumann
summary: Dirac's rule {f,g} → [f̂,ĝ]/iħ maps Hamiltonian mechanics onto Hilbert-space operators; conversely Koopman–von Neumann write classical mechanics as unitary evolution on L²(phase space).
breaks: Groenewold–van Hove: no quantization map preserves all brackets beyond quadratic polynomials.

name: Hamiltonian (hybrid) Monte Carlo
summary: HMC proposes moves by integrating fictitious Hamiltonian dynamics with leapfrog; time reversibility and Liouville volume preservation make the Metropolis correction exact.

name: Molecular dynamics integrates Hamilton's equations
summary: MD is numerical Hamiltonian mechanics for N particles; Nosé's extended Hamiltonian adds a thermostat variable so that the deterministic flow samples the canonical ensemble.
sources: Verlet (1967). "Computer 'Experiments' on Classical Fluids. I. Thermodynamical Properties of Lennard-Jones Molecules". *Phys. Rev.* 159, 98. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.159.98](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.159.98)
Nosé (1984). "A unified formulation of the constant temperature molecular dynamics methods". *J. Chem. Phys.* 81, 511. [doi:10.1063/1.447334](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.447334)

name: Conformal maps for 2D potential flow and lift
summary: Planar irrotational incompressible flow is an analytic complex potential; Joukowski conformal maps generate airfoils and the Blasius contour integral gives the Kutta–Joukowski lift.

name: Kelvin circulation from particle-relabelling symmetry
summary: In the Lagrangian (Euler–Poincaré) formulation of ideal fluids, invariance under relabelling of fluid particles is a Noether symmetry whose charge is circulation; Kelvin's theorem and potential-vorticity conservation follow.
breaks: Exact only for ideal barotropic fluids; viscosity and baroclinic torques break it.

name: Kuramoto sync and Turing patterns as symmetry breaking
summary: Kuramoto synchronization is a U(1)-breaking transition with order parameter re^{iψ} and mean-field exponent 1/2; Turing patterns spontaneously break translation symmetry.
breaks: Driven-dissipative attractors with no free energy or detailed balance; the phase mode diffuses rather than propagating, and noise can restore the symmetry.

name: Elasticity as the Goldstone theory of broken translations
summary: A crystal breaks continuous translations; continuum elasticity is the effective theory of the corresponding Goldstone fields (displacements), and its sound waves are the Goldstone modes.
breaks: Broken rotations give no independent Goldstone modes (inverse Higgs); amorphous solids are elastic without long-range order.

name: Resonant sensors: Q, bandwidth and thermal force noise
summary: Mechanical and electrical resonators used as sensors are driven damped oscillators; Q sets the bandwidth f₀/Q and the lock-in readout, and via fluctuation–dissipation the thermal force-noise floor.

name: Variational integrators and Ritz–Galerkin
summary: Discretizing the action rather than the equations gives variational integrators that are automatically symplectic and momentum-conserving (discrete Noether); finite elements are Ritz minimization of an energy functional.

name: Energy-based neural PDE solvers (Deep Ritz)
summary: Networks can minimize the variational energy of a mechanics problem instead of a residual, turning the principle of minimum potential energy into the training objective.
sources: Samaniego et al. (2020). "An energy approach to the solution of partial differential equations in computational mechanics via machine learning: Concepts, implementation and applications". *Comput. Methods Appl. Mech. Eng.* 362, 112790. [arXiv:1908.10407](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10407)

name: Liouville, recurrence and the arrow of time
summary: Time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian flow preserves phase-space volume, so fine-grained Gibbs entropy is constant and Poincaré recurrence holds; irreversibility needs coarse-graining plus a low-entropy past.

name: Least squares born from orbit determination
summary: Gauss developed least squares and the normal error law to recover the orbit of Ceres (1801–1809); χ² fitting of orbital elements remains the template for parameter estimation.

name: Galileo's square–cube law
summary: Galileo's 1638 argument that beam strength scales as L² while weight scales as L³ is the first scaling law and limits the size of animals and structures; Euler buckling follows the same logic.
